## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_inventory` retries up to 8 times. That breaks the project's 3-attempt retry cap, and the exemption this pull request adds to the rules file cannot authorise its own change, so this should be fixed before merge.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py`, an inventory fetcher that tries up to 8 times, and `app/health.py`, a health probe that tries up to 3 times. Both raise HTTP errors immediately and retry other `OSError`s. It also adds tests for both modules and a line in `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap fetch_inventory at 3 attempts per retry policy — When the legacy service is unreachable, `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8` with `timeout=10` and `RETRY_DELAY = 1.0` holds the caller for about 87 seconds. This breaks the rule "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (docs/review-rules.md:5). The exemption at docs/review-rules.md:7 is added by this same pull request, so it is a proposed change and not an existing rule. — During an outage of the legacy upstream, worker threads stay blocked for more than a minute per call, which is the failure the rule was written to prevent. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` and change the `fetch` case in `tests/test_retries.py:11`, or get the docs/review-rules.md:7 exemption approved as its own policy change that explains how the thread-holding risk is handled.
